title: SAP Automotive JIT Call Control Operations Playbook

meta.summary: Operational design guide for classic and Next Generation SAP Automotive JIT call control: actions, cancellation, monitoring, scanner use, handling units, transactions, programmatic interfaces, and recovery.

provenance.method: Grounded in SAP Help and converted into project-oriented design patterns. Project patterns are separated from standard SAP behavior.

mental_model: Call Control is a state/action engine. A status tells where the call is. An action changes business state and may create or reverse logistics side effects.
A status jump is not a business reversal. Emergency status correction can change status without undoing delivery, HU, goods movement, warehouse, transport, supplier-call, or billing objects.
Cancellation is an unwind process. Start from the latest irreversible or externally visible side effect and move backwards.

For JIS, the physical object matters as much as the SAP document. A packed rack, scanned HU, loaded truck, or forwarded Tier-2 call can make an electronic cancellation too late for automatic processing.

next_generation_action_patterns.interlinked_action_rule: SAP supports interlinked actions that execute two or more actions together. In Next Generation JIT, interlinked actions cannot be nested.

three_meanings_to_separate.question: Does the OEM or planner no longer need the call?
three_meanings_to_separate.result: Demand should no longer be active.

three_meanings_to_separate.question: Which physical/logistics objects already exist?
three_meanings_to_separate.result: Reverse or reconcile delivery, HU, warehouse task, goods movement, freight, confirmation, billing, or supplier call.

three_meanings_to_separate.question: Is SAP status wrong because processing failed?
three_meanings_to_separate.result: Use controlled correction only after checking real side effects.

recommended_unwind_order: Freeze automatic follow-on processing for the affected call/component group.
Read action log and linked documents before changing anything.
If billing exists, reverse billing first when the business process requires it.
If goods issue exists, reverse goods issue before cancelling or changing the delivery.
If warehouse tasks or EWM execution exist, cancel or reverse them according to warehouse state.
If an HU is packed or loaded, reconcile packing/HU assignment. Do not only change JIT status.
If delivery exists, cancel/delete/reject it using the supported logistics process for that release.
If a Tier-2 or outbound proxy call was created, send or execute the corresponding cancellation/change.
If production/backflush was posted, reverse or compensate it using the manufacturing/inventory process.
Only then move the JIT call/component group to the intended cancelled or reopened state.
Re-read linked documents and action logs to prove that logical and physical state are consistent.

classic_project_pattern.name: Mass cancellation / unwind report
classic_project_pattern.why_projects_build_it: One call can already have several side effects and users need a safe mass process instead of manually opening many transactions.
minimum_features: selection by external call number, customer, plant, component group, sequence range and current status
simulation mode that shows every planned reversal step
dependency checks for delivery, HU, goods issue, material document, forwarded call and billing
step-by-step action execution with commit boundaries
authority check and four-eyes approval for dangerous ranges
application log with before/after state and document references
no direct status-table update as the normal path
classic_project_pattern.implementation_hint: Prefer standard JIT actions, BAPIs/RFCs and logistics APIs. Use status correction only as an emergency tool, not as the engine of the cancellation program.

status_jump_warning.classic: Transaction JITE can change external/internal statuses without Call Control and without executing actions.
status_jump_warning.next_generation: Emergency status correction can also change processing/status indicators without normal business dependencies.
status_jump_warning.lead_rule: A jump is safe only when all skipped business effects are either not relevant, already reversed, or explicitly reconciled.

programmatic_interfaces_and_reports.finding: SAP Help documents many transactions and action interfaces, but not one classic standard report that safely reverses an arbitrary multi-step JIT process. Treat a project-specific multi-step cancellation utility as custom orchestration unless the target system proves otherwise.

Compare JIT calls with delivery confirmations

Create/display transfer order in classic WM context
Transaction variants; useful to simplify scanner/operator screens
transaction_catalog.operations_rule: Transaction lists are release and architecture dependent. Use them as orientation for classic SAP GUI processes, not as a promise that the target system uses the same UI.

classic_triage_path.question: What is the current call/component-group status and which actions are allowed?
Which actions succeeded or failed, who triggered them, and what was the previous status?
classic_triage_path.prerequisite: Logging Active must be enabled in Call Control.

classic_triage_path.question: Did the inbound IDoc fail technically or during JIT business processing?
Which JIT header/component-group/component values were determined?
Does delivery, HU, material document, warehouse task, confirmation or billing state match JIT state?
What does the configured action network allow from the current state?
After reconciliation, is emergency status correction still needed?

next_generation: Monitor Customer JIT Calls apps expose action logs and application logs.
Action Log records action ID, before/after status, action status/source and user.
Monitor JIT Calls at component-material level can show plant, PSA, requirement date/time, internal status, control cycle and logs.
Emergency correction also exposes packing, production, delivery, HU and goods-issue status indicators. Use them for reconciliation before manual correction.
monitoring_and_logs.log_retention_note: Classic JIT action logs can be deleted with transaction JITLOGDEL. Before JIT archiving, SAP documents saving logs through application-log archiving using object JIT and subobject Action.

classic_barcode_pattern.identity: Barcode qualifier + identifier. The qualifier defines which business attribute identifies the scanned object.
classic_barcode_pattern.entry_unit: The operator can scan several objects and execute one action. Entry unit can match rack capacity so the action fires automatically when the rack is full.
classic_barcode_pattern.screen_simplification: Use SHD0 transaction variants to hide fields and reduce operator choices.
classic_barcode_pattern.design_rule: The scanner should identify the physical object and request a business action. It should not write a status directly.

subsystem_pattern.use_case: MES, line terminal or custom scanner app reports a physical event.
recommended_flow: resolve it to JIT call/component group
check current internal status and allowed action
execute the JIT action through supported interface
print or update label only after committed success

ewm_rf_pattern.use: RF devices can support packing and HU processing in EWM.
ewm_rf_pattern.operational_model: Operator logs on to a packing work center, scans pick HUs, and the system can propose or create destination HUs depending on packing setup.
ewm_rf_pattern.jit_link: In Next Generation JIT, picking-started/completed and warehouse cancellation can update JIT Action Control. The warehouse becomes a source of physical truth, not only a downstream black box.

handling_unit_playbook.definition: A Handling Unit is a uniquely identified physical package made of packaging material plus packed products. HUs can be nested and have scannable IDs.
handling_unit_playbook.why_jis_cares: Sequence is physically carried by racks/HUs. A correct call status with the wrong HU sequence is still a line-side failure.

classic_patterns.pattern: Create HU automatically with sequenced JIT delivery
classic_patterns.configuration: Delivery control profile can enable HU generation.

classic_patterns.pattern: Create delivery for summarized call with HU
Assign an already built HU to summarized JIT call

reconciliation_checks: HU exists and is not already consumed/deleted.
HU contains the expected material/configuration and quantity.
HU sequence/rack position matches current JIS sequence.
HU is assigned to the expected delivery/warehouse process.
Loading or goods issue has not made repacking impossible.
A cancellation/change has a physical instruction for the operator, not only a SAP status change.

logistics_dependency_map.relation: commercial/planning anchor refined by short-horizon execution demand
call structure and operational control unit
Call Control releases and confirms work
delivery creation according to action/status and grouping rules
shipping execution and stock ownership change
customer confirmation can be matched back to JIT quantities
supplier/source and replenishment context for supply-to-production/outbound JIT
source, destination, PSA, timing and action-control determination
derived short-horizon demand with traceability to OEM requirement
picking and physical execution can update JIT statuses
modern forwarded-JIS process can create/modify/cancel freight units

project_actions_worth_considering.name: Z_HOLD
project_actions_worth_considering.purpose: Park call/component group during investigation without pretending it is cancelled.

project_actions_worth_considering.name: Z_RELEASE_HOLD
project_actions_worth_considering.purpose: Return a held object to controlled processing after checks.

project_actions_worth_considering.name: Z_QA_BLOCK
project_actions_worth_considering.purpose: Stop progression for quality issue and make operator reason visible.

project_actions_worth_considering.name: Z_REPACK_REQUIRED
project_actions_worth_considering.purpose: Mark that logical resequence needs physical HU/rack correction before shipping.

project_actions_worth_considering.name: Z_CANCEL_CHAIN
project_actions_worth_considering.guardrail: Simulation, idempotency and linked-document checks required.

project_actions_worth_considering.name: Z_RETRY_SAFE
project_actions_worth_considering.purpose: Retry one failed action only after verifying previous side effects.

project_actions_worth_considering.name: Z_NOTIFY_MES
project_actions_worth_considering.purpose: Publish state transition to shop-floor system after commit.

project_actions_worth_considering.name: Z_NOTIFY_3PL
project_actions_worth_considering.purpose: Notify external warehouse/service provider when call state requires physical action.

project_actions_worth_considering.name: Z_PRINT_EXCEPTION
project_actions_worth_considering.purpose: Print a clear exception/rack label for physical segregation.

lead_assessment_prompts: What is the difference between CANC, a multi-step cancellation procedure, and emergency status correction?
How do you cancel a call that already has delivery, HU and goods issue?
Why is an interlinked action safer than a direct status jump?
How would you design a scanner flow so that one scan cannot move the wrong rack?
Which logs do you check before reprocessing a failed action?
How do scheduling agreement, JIT call, component group, HU and delivery relate?
What changes when EWM or TM owns part of the physical execution?
How would you make a mass-cancellation report restartable after partial failure?

source_boundary.standard_sap_facts: Action names, transaction codes, documented BAPIs/RFC, standard reports, status-correction behavior, HU/JIT patterns and Next Generation interlinked cancellation are based on SAP Help.
source_boundary.project_synthesis: Cancellation unwind order, custom utility requirements, Z-action examples, scanner UX rules and assessment framing are practitioner-oriented design synthesis, not claims about one SAP standard implementation.
source_boundary.review_rule: Verify target S/4HANA release, deployment model, enabled JIT generation, EWM/TM architecture and customer-specific enhancements before using these details in a real specification.
